newsitem.title: USA: U.S. oil stocks rally on analyst's bullish comment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil stocks rally on analyst's bullish comment.

text.p: Oil stocks staged a dramatic rally, after Dean Witter's analyst made bullish comments about several stocks in the group and the outlook for crude oil prices.
Among the gainers, on heavy trading, were the three oil stocks that are components of the Dow Jones Industrial average -- which closed at or near their 52-week highs.
Analyst Eugene Nowak changed his Atlantic Richfield Co rating to accumulate from neutral and reiterated his buy recommendation on Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp . Texaco and Chevron are Dow Industrials.
The stock price gains came despite a decline in oil prices, which turned lower Thursday afternoon.

Traders said the decline came after the NYMEX crude oil contract failed to break key technical resistance of $26.80 per barrel, crude's post-Gulf War high, while losses in gasoline weighed on the oil complex generally.

Texaco closed up 2-7/8 to 104-7/8 after trading as high as 106 on volume of 1.6 million shares. Chevron closed at 68-1/4, up 1-7/8, on volume of 1.4 million shares. And Exxon closed at its session high of 103-1/4 -- a new 52-week high -- up 3-3/4 on trading of nearly 2.4 million shares.
Nowak said Tuesday's strength in the oil stocks was "maybe an over reaction to our morning comments" which said the "crude oil price outlook is very constructive."

He said "Demand for crude oil continues to be strong." Nowak said he now believes the average spot price for West Texas Intermediate -- the benchmark crude oil in the U.S. -- in 1997 will be toward the $21/barrel end of the $20-$21 range he had seen, "with some possible upside."
The 1996 average "appears to be coming in around $21.80 per barrel," he added.
"We expect any decline in oil prices to be gradual, which should importantly assist a refining and marketing recovery."

Recent downard pressure on Arco's share price "is presenting a favorable purchasing opportunity," Nowak said, raising the stock to accumulate from neutral while cutting his estimate of its fourth quarter earnings $0.10/share to $2.95, putting his 1996 year estimate at $9.95.
Nowak said his estimate of Arco's 1997 earnings was raised to $9.50 from $9.25 and he now sees it having earnings over $10 per share in 1999.
